findings.reason: the two most damaging categories are the ones a whole-file write destroys (a figure topic directory and a spliced evidence record), and the gate as written measures neither.
findings.text: s22's deliverable enumerates five exclusive patterns (plans, generated state, cumulative evidence records, figure topic directories, dependency locks) but its done-when plants only "a path matching an exclusive pattern", so a node that refuses one category and lets a write into a figure topic directory or a cumulative evidence record through passes the whole gate

findings.reason: without a case whose finished reviews outnumber the width, the node's gate cannot show the cap exists, and an uncapped sweep is the same unbounded promotion storm the section exists to end.
findings.text: s25's done-when runs four finished reviews against a configured width and asserts they "run concurrently up to the width", but it never configures a width smaller than four, so an implementation with no cap at all passes every case while the deliverable requires "promotions run concurrently up to a configured width"

findings.reason: a worker reading s22 will remove the pre-dispatch estimate with no replacement, and the admission refusals s23 and s24 describe return with nothing in the plan saying what sizes a node before it runs.
findings.text: s22's Why lists "the context estimate" among the jobs that "can be computed from the diff once it exists, or replaced by a fixed project-wide list", yet s23 and s24 state that nodes were refused on the local lane because the context estimate exceeded the 230k-token window, which means the estimate is consumed at admission, before any diff exists
